# Introduction

Two documents are considered near-duplicates if they are similar to each other.
An efficient and optimized algorithm for near-duplicates detection in a dataset is crucial for tasks like web crawling and, recently, cleaning datasets for AI models training. 
Manku et al. paper suggests to extract features from documents, compute the aggregated fingerprint using Charikar's Simhash and lastly compare fingerprints looking only at a specific partition of bits, for every partition.
This paper reproduces the central claims of [@original_paper] and analyzes its performance under different datasets, feature models and K values.
